decision: Add render to LUCA_READ_VERBS alongside summary/gate
alternatives: leave render unclassified (falls to luca-write conservative path)
reasoning: all three confidence reporters are stdout-only (confidence.ts:6-10, :281-288); context.md AI-owned call; verb-equality invariant catches future colliding-noun drift
risk: a future noun reusing verb 'render' with write semantics would classify bash-readonly; mitigated by completeness test

decision: Hoist subCommands literal into exported const CLI_SUBCOMMANDS; pass into defineCommand
alternatives: export the whole main command def; static source parse of cli.ts in the test
reasoning: smallest export surface; keeps import side-effect-free (lazy thunks unchanged); research rejected static parse as fragile
risk: citty SubCommandsDef typing friction at hoist site; caught by tsc gate

decision: Pin DELIBERATELY_UNCLASSIFIED to exactly {hook} and add ac-09.1 grep probe on that literal
alternatives: unpinned exclusion set (test could pass by dumping nouns into it)
reasoning: invariant-1 alone is gameable; pinning makes completeness proof sound
risk: future legitimate exclusion requires editing test + plan tombstone; acceptable friction

decision: Typed CLI_SUBCOMMANDS with 'satisfies SubCommandsDef' rather than a const-annotation
reasoning: satisfies validates against citty's contract while preserving literal key types, so the Wave 2 registry test can enumerate exact noun keys; an annotation would widen keys to Record<string,...>
risk: If citty's SubCommandsDef shape changes, the satisfies check surfaces it at typecheck — low risk

decision: Invariant-2 resolver awaits each noun thunk, unwraps an optional module-default return, and resolves possibly-lazy subCommands before sorted-array key equality; nouns absent from CLI_SUBCOMMANDS return early so invariant 3 reports the missing noun by name.
alternatives: assume thunks always return the CommandDef directly with no default unwrap
fail invariant 2 immediately on a missing noun instead of deferring to invariant 3
reasoning: All 16 noun thunks in cli.ts resolve named exports directly, but doctor uses m.default, so a future noun thunk may too; defensive unwrap is harmless for plain CommandDefs. Deferring missing-noun failures to invariant 3 keeps each failure named after the invariant that owns it.
risk: If a future noun exports both a CommandDef and a default key the unwrap could pick the wrong object; verb-set equality would then fail loudly rather than pass silently.

decision: Skipped SF2 -v anchor fix: the -v regression test is pre-existing (not in the staged diff); applied SF3 ReadonlySet/Readonly typing to all three exported registries (no consumer churn — has/spread/keys all ReadonlySet-compatible)
reasoning: Instructions scoped the -v fix to 'if present in the staged diff scope'; git diff HEAD shows the -v test only as unchanged context. SF3 typing compiled clean (tsc exit 0), so no churn conflict.
risk: Reviewer may have intended the -v fix regardless of diff scope
